To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the microbiome, the immune system, and the brain are in continuous communication, and that this dialogue can be altered by stress, and in the case of the gut microbiome, by early life microbial exposure.
the gut microbiota is involved in the regulation of the immune system and that this is relevant for brain function.
the microbiome, immunity, and behavior are linked in a dynamic and complex network of communication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between the gut microbiome, immune system, and the central nervous system.
the role of the immune system in the gut-brain axis and the impact that the microbiota has on this axis.
the role of the microbiome and the gut-brain axis in the pathophysiology of stress-related psychopathology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gut microbiota is an important factor in the development of the immune system and the brain and thus may be a key factor in the development and treatment of mental disorders.
the gut microbiota and immune system are key communication pathways between the gut and the brain, which plays a critical role in stress-related psychiatric disorders.
gut microbes play an important role in the immune-nervously system dialogue and that this is a key pathway in mediating the effect of stress on mental health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gut microbiota is an important mediator of stress and stress-related disorders and that the gut microbiome can be manipulated to improve mental health.
there are a number of potential sites of communication between the gut microbiota and the central nervous system.

the immune system, the gut microbiota and the central nervous system are in a continuous communication network that is critical in the development of the brain, and in maintaining homeostasis in adulthood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gut microbiota is an integral part of the immune system and that the immune system can have a significant impact on brain functioning.
the immune system, and in particular the gut, is a key communication hub between the brain and the microbiota.
the immune system plays a key role as a conduit of communication between the gut microbiota and brain and that this communication is altered in a range of psychiatric disorders.
